steps.do: Install Vue test tools as dev dependencies so the spec can run.
Create the component file SortableTable.vue inside the components folder.
In the template, wrap the body rows in TransitionGroup with tag set to tbody, name set to row, and each row keyed by row.id.
In the style block, add a row-move rule with transition transform 200ms ease.
Confirm the row-move class is defined in the component.
Run the spec that checks the moved rows get the row-move class during a sort.

K-018254.example: Sorting five rows by price gives each tr a 200ms transform slide, and grep prints 34: .row-move { transition: transform 200ms ease; }. The tag set to tbody keeps the markup valid, since TransitionGroup would otherwise render a div inside the table.
K-018254.check: grep prints one matching line with row-move, and vitest prints 1 passed with exit code 0.
traps: Rows without a stable key do not animate, because Vue reuses DOM nodes by index.
Leaving out tag tbody makes TransitionGroup render a div or span inside table, which breaks the markup.
Writing the class as v-move while name is row leaves the rule unused.

steps.do: Find the TransitionGroup element in the table component to confirm where the fade classes apply.

Create the browser test file that adds a row and measures its opacity over time.
Run the browser test for row fades in Chromium.
Check that the removed row is gone from the DOM within 200ms.

K-018255.example: Clicking Add row inserts a tr that starts at opacity 0 and reaches opacity 1 in 150ms. Clicking Remove keeps the row in the DOM for 150ms while it fades to opacity 0, then Vue deletes it.
K-018255.check: Playwright prints 1 passed, and the test records the row gone from the DOM at or under 200ms.
traps: A CSS duration that differs from the 200ms test limit makes the test flaky.
Naming the classes v-enter-from while name is row means the row-enter-from rule never runs.
A leaving row stays in the DOM until the transition ends, so tests must wait instead of checking at once.

steps.do: Search the project for existing reduced-motion rules so the new rule matches them.
Add a media query for prefers-reduced-motion reduce to the motion stylesheet that sets transition to none on row-move, row-enter-active, and row-leave-active.
In SortableTable.vue, create a ref that holds window.matchMedia with the query prefers-reduced-motion reduce and listen for its change event.
Bind the TransitionGroup css prop to the inverse of that ref so JavaScript hooks run without CSS transitions when reduced motion is set.
Run the browser test that emulates reduced motion and reads the computed transition duration of a row.

K-018256.example: The test calls page.emulateMedia with reducedMotion set to reduce, then reads getComputedStyle on a tr and expects transition-duration 0s. grep finds the media query in src/styles/motion.css at line 12, which shows the rule is present.
K-018256.check: Playwright prints 1 passed, and the computed transition-duration is 0s for every animated row.
traps: A CSS media query alone does not stop Vue JavaScript hooks, so the css prop must also be set.
matchMedia returns a value that does not update unless you listen for changes, so a static check goes stale.
Reading window during setup breaks server rendering because window does not exist on the server.
